meta.description: Test read. A label-and-value row with an optional trailing element, description and text link. Read independently of the existing Inline Text page to measure whether the framework reproduces its own result.

verdict.title: Fix — the property model and the caption contrast
verdict.text: Every paint is bound and every text node styled. But Type multiplies the set by four for presets its own slot already covers, the three has-properties are built two different ways, and the description reads at 4.01:1.

overview.inContextNote: Rows on a transaction or account-detail screen: a label on the left, its value on the right, with a copy action, a status badge or a check where the row needs one. Sketched; no screenshot of a shipping screen was read in this pass.
overview.inContextAlt: A detail card listing three label-and-value rows: the first with a copy icon, a description and a CTA link, the second with a status badge, the third with a checkmark.

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: Any label-and-value pair on a detail or receipt screen. Label, value, description and link are all content, and the trailing element is a slot, so nothing in the set is tied to one product.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Owns its layout and every text layer; the trailing element comes from its own Trailing Elements component. All 64 visible paints are bound to variables and all 52 text nodes carry a DS style, so it depends on nothing unbound.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: The copy is identical across all 16 variants and the tokens hold throughout. What breaks: three has… properties built two ways — two string variants, one boolean — and a 2px right inset on the supporting row that appears only when description and link are both shown.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: The trailing element is an instance of Trailing Elements, the badge an instance of Badge, the icons DS icon instances. Nothing is redrawn locally.

behavior.notes: A 24 × 24 copy icon after the value, #445C85 at 1.8, back sheet at 40%. The icon is the copy action; no pressed state is drawn.
A 48 × 18 Badge instance after the value: #E5F1FF pill, #005CE5 label, radius 99.
A 16 × 16 check, one path at #445C85, stroke 3. Display only.
An empty 24 × 24 Slot — space is reserved, nothing is drawn until content is placed.
Hides Trailing Elements in all 16 variants — read from the layer binding, not inferred.
The CTA link is tappable but no pressed or disabled look is built for it, or for the copy icon.

open.headline: The Type axis multiplies the set for presets its own slot covers.
open.body: Each Type value only sets the nested Trailing Elements instance's own Type — and Type=Slot already accepts any trailing content. Copy Icon, Badge and Checkmark are presets of that slot, yet they multiply the set by four. The names do not match either: Copy Icon here, Icon on the nested instance.

open.headline: Three has… properties, built two different ways.
open.body: hasDescription and hasTextLink are VARIANT properties with string values True / False; hasTrailingElement is a real BOOLEAN. Their value order disagrees too — False | True on one, True | False on the other. The two variants remove their layer outright; the only thing a boolean could not reproduce is the link right-aligning when it stands alone.

open.headline: The description reads at 4.01:1.
open.body: Description is #6780A9, Secondary/Bold/Caption at 12px, on a white surface — 4.01:1, under the 4.5:1 that 12px text needs. Computed from the read fill with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. The label (14.6:1), value (6.74:1), link (5.73:1) and badge (5.01:1) all pass.

open.headline: The link is a 21 × 18 target with no pressed state.
open.body: LinkLabel draws at 21 × 18, under the 24 × 24 minimum of WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 unless the spacing around it makes up the difference, and well under the 44 pt a native platform expects. Neither the link nor the copy icon has a pressed or disabled look.

open.headline: A 2px inset appears only when description and link are both shown.
open.body: SupportingRow has 0 padding in every variant except the eight with both description and link, where it carries 2 on the right. So the link sits 2px inside the trailing element's edge in those eight, and flush with it everywhere else.

recommendations.headline: Collapse Type into the trailing slot.
recommendations.body: Keep one Inline Text with a trailing slot and ship Copy Icon, Badge and Checkmark as preferred instances of Trailing Elements. The set drops from 16 variants to 4, and a new trailing element needs no new variant.

recommendations.headline: Make every has… a boolean.
recommendations.body: Turn hasDescription and hasTextLink into BOOLEAN properties like hasTrailingElement, and let SupportingRow use space-between so the link keeps its right edge on its own.

recommendations.headline: Name the value after the nested one.
recommendations.body: Use Icon on both levels, or Copy Icon on both. A value that changes name one level down is one more lookup for every developer mapping it.

recommendations.headline: Raise the description to 4.5:1.
recommendations.body: The description carries the context for the value — a date, a reference, a condition — so it is information, not decoration.

recommendations.headline: Give the link and the copy action a hit area and a pressed state.
recommendations.body: State the tappable area separately from the drawn text (44 pt is the safe native answer) and draw a pressed look for both actions, so each platform does not invent its own.

recommendations.headline: Drop the 2px inset or apply it everywhere.
recommendations.body: Either the link aligns to the trailing column or it does not; today it depends on whether a description is present.

accessibility.requirement: Label and value read as one
accessibility.ios: Combine the row with .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) so VoiceOver reads "Label, 0.00" once.
The copy icon is a Button with accessibilityLabel("Copy Label"), and a confirmation is announced after copying.
accessibility.android: IconButton with contentDescription = "Copy $label"; announce the result through a liveRegion or a snackbar.

accessibility.ios: Give the CTA a 44 × 44 pt tappable frame with .contentShape, independent of its 21 × 18 drawn text.
accessibility.android: Use Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize() so the link reaches 48 dp.

accessibility.ios: Give the check an accessibilityLabel("Verified"); it is otherwise a silent decoration.
The badge label is part of the combined row element, not a separate stop.
accessibility.android: Include the badge text in the merged semantics of the row.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use Inline Text for a label and its value on a detail or receipt screen.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not use it for editable values — it is display only, with a link or copy action at most.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use Type=Copy Icon when the user is likely to paste the value elsewhere, such as a reference number.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not add a copy icon to a value that cannot be pasted usefully, like a status.

usageGuidelines.doText: Keep the description to one line of context for the value.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not put instructions in the description; it reads at caption size and below the contrast minimum today.

scorecard.notes: Clear, role-named frames — MainRow, ValueGroup, SupportingRow, DescriptionGroup — and every text layer named for its content. The one wrinkle: SupportingRow carries 2 right padding in only the eight variants that show both description and link.

The whole property panel was read over REST, boolean included. Type duplicates the nested instance's own type under a different value name (Copy Icon vs Icon) and multiplies the set by four; hasDescription and hasTextLink are string variants while hasTrailingElement is a boolean, with their value orders reversed.

Measured, not assumed: all 64 visible paints across the 16 variants carry a bound variable, and all 52 text nodes carry a DS text style — Primary/Label/Light/Base, Primary/Label/Fine, Secondary/Bold/Caption. The variable names themselves still need a Dev Mode read; the five ids are listed under the colors table.
Label and value map to two strings, description and link to two optional parameters, and the trailing element to one enum with a custom case. Nothing forces iOS and Android apart.

The component is mostly display, but it carries two actions — the CTA link and the copy icon — and neither has a pressed or disabled look. The link draws at 21 × 18, under the 24 × 24 minimum, and the description reads at 4.01:1.
Both icons export as clean stroked paths bound to #445C85 — the copy icon as two sheets at 1.8, the check as one path at 3 — with the icon-template grid hidden. The badge is a DS Badge instance.

rows.body: Independent trial read of Inline Text, run against the refined framework. The component already has a page at Inline Text; this one was written from a fresh read without consulting it. It stays out of the sidebar, search, the grid and the counts.

First test to use both toolchains. The Figma REST API supplied the full property panel (the boolean hasTrailingElement included), auto-layout padding, gap and alignment, text-style names, bound variable ids and the layer-to-property bindings — so no Layout row is left unread. The Talk To Figma plugin supplied the PNG and SVG exports.
The plugin's get_node_info omitted the checkmark's one visible vector from its child list; REST returned it. The layer tree from either tool is checked against an export before it is written down.

Contrast ratios are computed from the read fills with the WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance formula, on a white surface. Token names are unread: the variables sit in a library, and neither toolchain can name library variables from this file.
